status.summary: Retired. The two-time former UFC heavyweight champion lost to Jon Jones at UFC 309 in New York (Nov 16, 2024), TKO at 4:29 of round 3 after a spinning back kick to the body, and said after the fight that he was done fighting. It was his first fight since losing the title to Francis Ngannou at UFC 260 (Mar 27, 2021). Age 44. No UFC bout appears in the UFC Stats snapshot of Oct 31, 2026. Any 2025-26 news (honours, comeback talk) was NOT verified this session (web search budget used up; Wikipedia and ufc.com blocked).
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_Miocic (reference for the post-fight retirement; not reachable this session, so unverified)

signature: jab and straight right; right-hand counters finished Fabricio Werdum (UFC 198, R1 2:47) and Junior dos Santos (UFC 211, R1 2:22) for his title win and second defence (UFC Stats: punch to head in clinch)
body attack that turned the Daniel Cormier rematch: 14 of 16 body strikes landed in round 4 at UFC 241 before the TKO at 4:09
takedowns into long top control and ground strikes: 6 takedowns and 15:02 of control vs Francis Ngannou (UFC 220); 6 of 8 takedowns, 16:27 of control and 57 ground strikes vs Mark Hunt (2015)
ground-and-pound finishes: Overeem (UFC 203, punches from guard), Hunt (R5, punches on the ground), Shane del Rosario (elbows from half guard)
five-round pace for a heavyweight: 13 five-round UFC fights, with output in rounds 2-4 at 1.06-1.13 times round 1
weaknesses: four KO/TKO losses: Stefan Struve (2012), Cormier (UFC 226, punches in the clinch, R1), Ngannou (UFC 260, R2 0:52) and Jones (UFC 309, R3)
age and rust: 42 and three and a half years out at UFC 309, where Jones out-landed him 96-37 and he attempted no takedowns
no submission game: 0 submission attempts in 19 UFC fights
gets hit in exchanges: 4.0 significant strikes absorbed per minute career (heavyweight median 3.6), rising to 5.6 recency-weighted
takedown accuracy only 34% (Junior dos Santos stopped 17 of 18 shots in 2014)
style.summary: A heavyweight wrestle-boxer with a Division I wrestling base: a busy jab and straight right, counters going backwards, a late body attack and takedowns into long spells on top with ground strikes. In his title years he out-landed and out-wrestled the division (4.7 significant strikes per minute, 1.7 takedowns per 15 min), but he was knocked out four times and looked his age against Jones in his last fight.

moves.notes: Group weights (head, body, leg) each sum to 1; the engine's target split should come from fighters.json. Career significant attempts go head 0.844 / body 0.083 / leg 0.073 and landed head 0.732 / body 0.138 / leg 0.130; recency-weighted attempts are 0.810 / 0.111 / 0.079. League heavyweight attempts are about 0.78 / 0.13 / 0.10, so he is more head-focused than average and kicks little. The head group is jab and cross first (his finishes of Werdum and dos Santos were right hands; 72% of his landed significant strikes are at distance), then hook and some overhand; head kick is 0.02. The body group leans on hooks for the round-4 body attack on Cormier at UFC 241 (14 of 16 landed in that round); body accuracy is 87% career, so some of it is kicks (0.2). His leg strikes are occasional low kicks (17 of 17 vs Cormier at UFC 252, 16 of 17 vs Ngannou at UFC 220); the calf/inside split is a judgment. Elbow 0.15 reflects ground-and-pound (16% of his landed strikes are on the ground; elbow TKO of del Rosario). Knee small, spinning 0. UFC Stats does not record technique types, so the within-group split is an analyst judgment from the bout stats in data/raw.

engine_notes.note: Holds his pace into round 4: five-round pace relative to round 1 is 1.00 / 1.13 / 1.06 / 1.09 / 0.85 over 13 five-round fights; three-round curve 1.00 / 1.15 / 1.11. He beat Cormier in round 4 and went 25 minutes three times in title fights.
Wrestling is a real threat at heavyweight: 1.74 takedowns per 15 min (heavyweight median 0.68) and 26.5% of fight time in control, while opponents controlled him only 5.1% of the time.
Power on both sides: 0.49 knockdowns scored per 15 min (median 0.27) and 0.42 absorbed; 9 KO/TKO wins and 4 KO/TKO losses in 19 UFC fights.

Recency-weighted sums cover only 15.8 minutes, mostly the Jones fight (37 landed vs 96 absorbed), so recency striking defence (33%) is far below career (52%). For a prime version use the career sums; for a current one shrink toward career and apply a large age (44) and inactivity discount.
